question: Explain the convolution theorem for Fourier transforms.
_instructions: For each step set 'human_correct' to true/false. Set 'error_type' to one of: algebra, sign, missing_term, substitution, definition, none. Set '_filled' to true when done. Set 'final_answer_correct' to true/false after comparing 'generated_final' to 'expected_final'.

steps.description: Define the Fourier transform of a signal x(t)
steps.notes: Standard FT definition with shorthand x for x(t). Acceptable notation.

steps.description: Define the Fourier transform of a signal y(t)
Define the convolution of x(t) and y(t) in the time domain
steps.expression_given: integrate(x.subs(t, t - tau) * y.subs(t, tau), (tau, -oo, oo))
steps.notes: Standard convolution integral (x*y)(t) = integral of x(t-tau)*y(tau) dtau. Correct.

steps.description: Take the Fourier transform of the convolution integral
steps.expression_given: integrate((integrate(x.subs(t, t - tau) * y.subs(t, tau), (tau, -oo, oo))) * exp(-I*omega*t), (t, -oo, oo))
steps.notes: Correctly wraps the convolution in the FT integral over t.

steps.expression_given: integrate(y.subs(t, tau) * integrate(x.subs(t, t - tau) * exp(-I*omega*t), (t, -oo, oo)), (tau, -oo, oo))
steps.notes: Valid by Fubini's theorem for absolutely integrable signals. Order of integration correctly swapped.

steps.description: Substitute variable in inner integral: let u = t - tau
steps.expression_given: integrate(y.subs(t, tau) * integrate(x * exp(-I*omega*(u + tau)), (u, -oo, oo)), (tau, -oo, oo))
steps.notes: u = t - tau => t = u + tau, dt = du, limits unchanged. Substitution is correct.

steps.description: Factor exponential in inner integral: exp(-I*omega*(u + tau)) = exp(-I*omega*u) * exp(-I*omega*tau)
steps.expression_given: integrate(y.subs(t, tau) * (exp(-I*omega*tau) * integrate(x * exp(-I*omega*u), (u, -oo, oo))), (tau, -oo, oo))
steps.notes: Correct factoring. exp(-I*omega*tau) is constant w.r.t. u and pulled out of inner integral.

steps.description: Recognize that the inner integral is the Fourier transform of x(t)
steps.notes: Inner integral over u of x*exp(-I*omega*u) is exactly X(omega) by definition. Correct identification.

steps.description: Factor out X since it is constant with respect to tau
steps.notes: X(omega) is independent of tau, so factoring out is valid.

steps.description: Recognize that the remaining integral is the Fourier transform of y(t)
steps.notes: Integral of y(tau)*exp(-I*omega*tau) dtau is Y(omega) by definition. Final result X*Y is correct.
